ROUND 2 — what changed

The shape is settled (domain cards). The rule is new: NUMBERS where items are interchangeable, ROWS only where each item is its own thing. So the cards are deliberately different shapes.

· Training — one line, in the strip and in its card
· Open orders — three counts (undercut / outbid / relist), no rows. Below-floor keeps a footer line of its own
· Mining tax — two counts: ISK unpaid, entries unassigned
· Planetary — one row per BATCH sharing a timer, not per colony
· Industry — real rows, kept as you liked it
· Alerts — grouped by notification type, count first

Fixed: "Owed to you" was backwards — the ledger records what you owe your payees. It now reads "You owe".

Dropped: the 48-hour bar chart, the merged action queue, the decayed-colony row.

THE PROOF

Same board, bad night: 137 undercut, 18 colonies with 6 expired, 341 alerts across 17 types, empty skill queue, two-day-old data.

Identical layout. Identical card heights. Nothing scrolled and nothing that mattered got pushed off — which is the thing the first round could not do.

THE ONE OPEN FORK

Alerts are a different volume class from everything else. Two answers:

MAIN — alerts take an ordinary card, show the worst three types, roll the rest into the footer. The board stays a board.

THIS — alerts get a column of their own, so a loud day never pushes the other cards around and you can dismiss in place.

Costs a third of the width every day to solve a problem you have some days.

STILL OPEN

1. Multi-character. All of this is the active character. The alert feed is device-wide. Should the board span every pilot, or stay one at a time?

2. Deep links. "Undercut 21" would open /market?section=orders — there is no route today that opens it pre-filtered to undercut, or that jumps to one colony. Worth adding?

3. Does this replace Overview, or sit above it? The wallet panel, skill-queue panel and three count tiles are all gone.

4. Is below-floor really a footer line, or does it deserve to be the fourth number?
